column1: # VENDORED.tsv - manifest for skills-vendor.sh (the OPS skill-mount mechanism).
# OPS mounts portable technique skills rather than carrying a drifting fork of
# each. The skill repos cloned under PROJECTS/ are the source of truth; this file
# lists which skill dirs are mirrored into SKILLS/ and from where. Edit a vendored
# skill at its source repo, then run `skills-vendor.sh sync` to refresh the mirror
# here. Never hand-edit the mirrored SKILLS/<name>/ dirs; the sync replaces them.
# A folder the sync did not write (your own skill under a name a row mounts, or
# a hand-edited mirror) is moved to .claude-config/backup/skills-replaced/ first,
# never deleted; SKILLS/.vendored-state.tsv records what the sync wrote.
# Format: one row per skill, tab-separated:
#   <name><TAB><source-dir relative to ~/OPS/PROJECTS>
# The mirror lands at ~/OPS/SKILLS/<name>/. Lines starting with # and blank lines
# are ignored. The drift gate is `skills-vendor.sh --check`, wired into
# verify-ops.sh (DRIFT = FAIL, MISSING = WARN).
# To mount a source, clone it under PROJECTS/<org>/<repo> first, add a row per
# skill below, then run: skills-vendor.sh sync
# The template ships no rows (2026-11-17). Its nine rows mounted the public
# Exploitacious/agent-skills set; the owner ruled those skills out of the
# template, because a shared skill lives in exactly one repo, and a template copy
# of a same-named skill (meta-skill-creator was one) blocks the shared one.
# Add rows for an org or private source of your own below, one per skill.
# Versions: this file has no version column. A mount follows the checked-out
# commit of its source clone, and deploy never pulls an existing clone, so you
# move to a newer release on purpose (SKILLS/README.md, "Skill sources").
# Every mounted skill costs its description in each session's skill listing
# (SKILLS/README.md, "The skill listing budget"). To stop mounting one, delete its
# row and its SKILLS/<name>/ mirror folder: sync writes mirrors and never removes
# one.
